concepts.def: Turning effect of a force about a point: moment = force × perpendicular distance from pivot. Units: Nm.
Body in equilibrium if resultant force = 0 AND resultant moment about any point = 0.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Moments — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Moments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Moments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A force of 10 N acts perpendicular to a rod, 0.5 m from the pivot. Moment is:
options: 5 Nm
20 Nm

mcqs.q: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of moments about any point is:
options: zero
positive
equal to weight × distance
depends on pivot

mcqs.q: If 6 workers take 8 hours to paint a wall, how long would 12 workers take (assuming they work at the same rate)?
options: 4 hours — this is inverse proportion: double the workers, halve the time.
8 hours, because each worker still has to do the same job.
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
16 hours, because doubling the workers doubles everything including the time.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between congruent and similar shapes?
options: Congruent shapes are identical in size and shape; similar shapes have the same shape but can be different sizes (scaled).
Congruent and similar both mean 'the same shape' — they're interchangeable.
Congruent shapes are similar with different angles.
8 hours, because each worker still has to do the same job.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of any pentagon?
options: 540 degrees — use (n - 2) x 180 with n = 5.
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
Congruent shapes are similar with different angles.
360 degrees, because all polygons' angles sum to one full turn.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Principle of moments”?
options: Beams on supports: each support provides a normal reaction. Use moments and force balance to find magnitudes.
Beam about to tip when reaction at one support becomes zero. Useful for limit-case problems.
Body in equilibrium if resultant force = 0 AND resultant moment about any point = 0.
For equilibrium, sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments about same point.

free_texts.q: What is the term for the turning effect of a force?

sequence.def: Turning effect = force × perpendicular distance — the core idea.
No net force and no net moment — the condition to apply.
Sum of clockwise = sum of anticlockwise moments.
Upward force from supports, found via equilibrium.
When reaction reaches zero an object topples — final application.
